newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP dips then bounces on profit slump.
newsitem.headline: BHP dips then bounces on profit slump.

text.p: Shares in The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd dipped and then bounced back in volatile late Friday morning trade after BHP posted a sharply lower year net profit of A$410 million, including an after-tax abnormal loss of A$976 million.
BHP's shares slid ten cents to A$18.87 just after the result was announced, but bounced back within five minutes to A$19.00, down six cents on Thursday's close.
The abnormal losses were due largely to a A$550 million writedown on some of its Magma copper assets in North America.
Pre-abnormal profits rose A$93 million to A$1.386 billion, compared with analysts forecasts of between A$1.35 billion to A$1.4 billion.
Brokers said the market welcomed BHP's decision to write-down the values of its copper, steel and minerals assets.
"I think the market was relieved that they're wiping the slate clean," said BNP Equities head of equities John Bowie Wilson, referring to a late morning rise in BHP's share price to A$19.12.
"People are regarding it as responsible management," Bowie Wilson said. "Otherwise it's market neutral," he said.
Intersuisse head of equities Andrew Sekely said the result appeared marginally better than expectations.
"They're certainly better than what the pessimists were predicting," Sekely said.
"People are coming to the view that although it's nothing startling, it does look as though it will be enough to hold it at these levels," he said.

BHP's share price has recovered from a 1997 low of A$16.45 low on April 1 in recent months, reaching a 1997 high of A$20.05 on June 20 despite a warning from BHP chief executive John Prescott on May 26 that the full year result would be below some
Rothschilds Australia head of equities Gerard Eakin said the result had been on expectations.
"It's nice to see there were no negative surprises within the released results," Eakin said.
"We don't think it's overpriced, but we also don't think it's an outstanding buy," he said, adding it was probably more likely the share price would continue to rise than fall.
"Given the differential with CRA, you wouldn't be suprised to see some switching in favour of BHP and out of CRA," he said.
Rio Tinto, which was down 29 cents at A$22.55 at 12.00 p.m. (0200 GMT), is trading at 17.4 times consensus earnings per share forecast for calendar 1998.
BHP was trading at around 18 times consensus forecast earnings per share for 1998 and over 20 times current earnings per share.
